`packet-tls-utils.h` include the header for `gnutls`:
```
#ifdef HAVE_LIBGNUTLS
#include <gnutls/x509.h>
#include <gnutls/pkcs12.h>
#endif /* HAVE_LIBGNUTLS */
```

For the build to work on Windows, had to add path to the `gnutls` includes:  
```
diff --git a/epan/wslua/CMakeLists.txt b/epan/wslua/CMakeLists.txt
index 2a0d4e0e29..8e724cecf8 100644
--- a/epan/wslua/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/epan/wslua/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -122,6 +122,7 @@ endif()
 target_include_directories(wslua
        SYSTEM PRIVATE
                ${GCRYPT_INCLUDE_DIRS}
+               ${GNUTLS_INCLUDE_DIRS}
                ${LUA_INCLUDE_DIRS}
        PRIVATE
                ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}
```

The wsluarm script does not handle the mixed case variable names.  
TLS_handle and APP_handle do not appear in WSDG.  
Changing the variables to TLS_HANDLE and APP_HANDLE adds them to the output.  
It's not clear to me if the input is a handle or a dissector.  


```
11.1.1.15. ssl_starttls_ack(pinfo)
TLS protocol will be started after this fame

Arguments
pinfo
The packet’s Pinfo.


11.1.1.16. ssl_starttls_post_ack(pinfo)
TLS protocol is started with this frame

Arguments
pinfo
The packet’s Pinfo.

----------------------------------------------------

11.1.1.15. ssl_starttls_ack(tls_handle, pinfo, app_handle)
TLS protocol will be started after this fame

Arguments
tls_handle
the tls dissector
pinfo
The packet’s Pinfo.
app_handle
The app dissector

11.1.1.16. ssl_starttls_post_ack(tls_handle, pinfo, app_handle)
TLS protocol is started with this frame

Arguments
tls_handle
the tls dissector
pinfo
The packet’s Pinfo.
app_handle
The app dissector
```
